title: Sep 10 Results: Tough Night in the Bullpen
summary: Sep 10 picks went 2-3 with 40% accuracy—breaking down what went wrong from the mound

content.value:
## The Reality Check

Look, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it—tonight was a rough outing. Going 2-3 with a 40% success rate is the kind of line that gets you sent down to Triple-A. As a former pitcher, I know what it's like when your best stuff just isn't working. You've got to own it, break down the tape, and figure out what went wrong.

## Game-by-Game Breakdown

Let me walk you through each pitch—err, pick—and what the numbers told us versus what actually happened on the field.

## What Went Wrong

From a pitcher's perspective, three misses in a row—Rays, Phillies, Rangers—that's like loading the bases with nobody out. All three were razor-thin margins, 50-54% confidence. In baseball, that's basically a coin flip. When you're dealing with that kind of variance, you need everything to break your way, and tonight it didn't.

The Yankees and Pirates picks saved us from a complete disaster. At 61% and 59% respectively, those were our higher-confidence calls, and they came through like veteran relievers in a tight spot.

## The Pitcher's Take

Here's the thing about probabilities that a lot of folks don't get: a 54% pick isn't a lock. It's like throwing a two-seam fastball with good movement—you're giving yourself the best chance, but sometimes the hitter just gets a piece of it. Three 50-54% picks going the wrong way? That's baseball. That's variance.

But make no mistake—40% isn't good enough. In the rotation, you need to be hitting your spots more consistently than this. We'll review the film, adjust the approach, and come back stronger.

content.title: ⚠️ Tomorrow's Schedule
content.sub: Off day for the entire league—time to rest and reset

content.value:
## The Silver Lining

With no games tomorrow, we've got time to do what every pitcher does after a rough outing: study, adjust, and get ready for the next appearance. Sometimes the best thing you can do is take a day to clear your head and come back with fresh eyes.

Stay locked in. We'll be back when the games resume.
